questions.concept: Money creation — new lending beyond the deposit
questions.stem: A customer deposits 500 in a bank. The reserve requirement is 20%. The amount of new lending the banking system can generate beyond the initial deposit is closest to:
questions.explanation: Total money (all deposits) = 500 / 0.20 = 2,500. The stem asks for lending BEYOND the initial deposit → 2,500 − 500 = 2,000. Choice C is the total; choice A is the first bank's reserve (500 × 0.20). Only subtract the original deposit when the stem says 'additional' / 'beyond' / 'new loans' — otherwise 'money created' means the whole 2,500.
questions.kr: 총 통화(모든 예금) = 500/0.20 = 2,500. '최초 예금을 넘어서는 신규 대출'을 물었으므로 2,500 − 500 = 2,000. C는 총액, A는 첫 은행의 지급준비금. '추가/beyond/신규 대출'이라고 할 때만 최초 예금을 빼고, 그 외 '창출된 통화'는 2,500 전체.

questions.stem: If the reserve requirement falls from 10% to 8%, the money multiplier most likely:

choices.A: falls from 10 to 8
choices.B: rises from 10 to 12.5
choices.C: is unchanged, since it depends on deposits

questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1 / reserve requirement: 1/0.10 = 10 → 1/0.08 = 12.5. A smaller reserve requirement means banks lend a larger share of each deposit → MORE money is created. Choice A treats the percentage as the multiplier; choice C confuses the multiplier (a ratio) with the total created (deposit × multiplier).
questions.kr: 승수 = 1/지급준비율: 1/0.10 = 10 → 1/0.08 = 12.5. 준비율이 낮을수록 예금의 더 큰 비율을 대출 → 통화 창출 증가. A는 퍼센트를 승수로 착각, C는 승수(비율)와 총 창출액(예금 × 승수)을 혼동.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to be part of narrow money?

choices.A: Notes and coins in circulation
choices.B: Highly liquid demand deposits
choices.C: Credit card balances

questions.explanation: Narrow money = notes and coins in circulation + very highly liquid deposits (A and B are TRUE members). A credit-card payment is a DEFERRED payment, not a transfer of a money balance — credit cards are not money at all, narrow or broad. Least-likely stem: T/F each option, pick the F.
questions.kr: 협의통화 = 유통 중인 지폐·주화 + 매우 유동적인 예금(A·B는 포함). 신용카드 결제는 '지급 이연'이지 통화 잔액의 이전이 아님 → 신용카드는 협의든 광의든 통화가 아님. least likely → 선지별 T/F 후 F 선택.

questions.stem: Money supply 800, velocity 5, real output 2,000. The price level is closest to:
questions.explanation: M × V = P × Y → 800 × 5 = 4,000 = P × 2,000 → P = 2.0. Choice A inverts the ratio (2,000/4,000); choice C divides nominal spending by velocity instead of output.

questions.stem: Under money neutrality, a 6% increase in the money supply with constant velocity will most likely raise:

choices.A: real output by 6%
choices.B: the price level by 6%
choices.C: velocity by 6%

questions.explanation: Neutrality: money affects neither real output (Y) nor velocity (V), so in MV = PY the entire 6% lands on P. Choice A is the short-run / non-neutral story; choice C contradicts the stem (velocity constant).
questions.kr: 중립성: 통화는 실질산출(Y)이나 유통속도(V)에 영향 없음 → MV = PY에서 6% 전부가 P로. A는 단기·비중립 이야기, C는 지문(유통속도 불변)과 모순.

questions.stem: Expected returns on bonds rise while their perceived risk is unchanged. The speculative demand for money will most likely:

choices.A: rise
choices.B: fall
choices.C: be unchanged

questions.explanation: Speculative balances are INVERSELY related to expected returns on other assets (holding money forgoes that return — the opportunity cost rose) and DIRECTLY related to their perceived risk. Returns up, risk unchanged → hold less money.
questions.kr: 투기적 화폐수요는 다른 자산의 기대수익률과 '역'관계(현금 보유의 기회비용 상승), 인지된 위험과는 '정'관계. 수익률↑·위험 불변 → 화폐 보유 감소.

questions.stem: The nominal interest rate is above its equilibrium level. The most likely adjustment is that agents:

choices.A: sell bonds, lowering bond prices and raising rates
choices.B: buy bonds, raising bond prices and lowering rates
choices.C: hold more money, raising rates

questions.explanation: Rate above equilibrium → quantity of money demanded is below the fixed supply → EXCESS SUPPLY of money → agents use the surplus balances to BUY bonds → bond prices rise → interest rates fall back to I₀. Choice A is the adjustment from BELOW equilibrium (excess demand → sell bonds). Bond price and interest rate always move inversely.
questions.kr: 금리가 균형 위 → 화폐수요량 < 고정된 공급 → 화폐 '초과공급' → 잉여 잔액으로 채권 '매수' → 채권가격↑ → 금리↓(균형으로). A는 균형 '아래'일 때의 조정(초과수요 → 채권 매도). 채권가격과 금리는 항상 반대.

questions.stem: The nominal interest rate is 7% and the required real rate is 3%. Expected inflation is closest to:
questions.explanation: R_nom = R_real + πᵉ → 7% = 3% + πᵉ → πᵉ = 4%. Choice A is the real rate itself; choice C adds instead of subtracting. It is EXPECTED inflation; realized inflation is the standard distractor.
questions.kr: 명목 = 실질 + 기대인플레이션 → 7 = 3 + πᵉ → 4%. A는 실질금리 자체, C는 뺄셈 대신 덧셈. '기대' 인플레이션이며 실현 인플레이션은 오답 유인.

questions.stem: Inflation turns out to be lower than was anticipated when a fixed-rate loan was agreed. Most likely:

choices.A: the borrower benefits at the lender's expense
choices.B: the lender benefits at the borrower's expense
choices.C: neither, since the rate was fixed

questions.explanation: Debt is fixed in nominal terms. Lower-than-expected inflation means the real value of the repayment is HIGHER than both sides priced in → the lender receives more purchasing power than expected → lender gains, borrower loses. (Higher-than-expected inflation is the mirror: borrower gains.) 'Fixed rate' is exactly why the surprise matters — it can't adjust.
questions.kr: 부채는 명목 고정. 인플레이션이 예상보다 낮으면 상환액의 실질가치가 양측이 가정한 것보다 '높음' → 대출자(lender)가 예상보다 많은 구매력을 받음 → 대출자 이득, 차입자 손해. (예상보다 높으면 반대: 차입자 이득.) 고정금리라서 오히려 서프라이즈가 중요.

questions.stem: According to the curriculum, the main reason unanticipated inflation can destabilize an economy is that it:

choices.A: raises the nominal cost of all goods
choices.B: reduces the information content of market prices
choices.C: is always higher than anticipated inflation

questions.explanation: The TV-manufacturer story: a +10% price rise is read as a RELATIVE signal (more demand for TVs) when it was a GENERAL rise → over-investment, then surplus and layoffs. Unanticipated inflation makes relative and general price changes indistinguishable → corrupted signals → exacerbated booms and busts. Choice A is true of any inflation and not the destabilizing mechanism; choice C is false (unexpected inflation can be above OR below).
questions.kr: TV 제조업체 사례: +10% 가격 상승을 '상대가격' 신호(TV 수요 증가)로 읽었지만 실제론 '일반 물가' 상승 → 과잉투자 → 재고·해고. 예상 밖 인플레이션은 상대 vs 일반 가격 변화를 구분 못 하게 함 → 신호 왜곡 → 호황·불황 증폭. A는 모든 인플레이션에 해당, C는 거짓(예상보다 낮을 수도 있음).

questions.stem: Which kind of inflation is most likely to be factored into wage negotiations and financial contracts?

choices.A: Unexpected inflation
choices.B: Expected inflation
choices.C: Uncertain inflation

questions.explanation: Fully anticipated (expected) inflation can be built into wage bargains and contract pricing, so it does little harm. Unexpected inflation is by definition the part that was NOT priced in; uncertain inflation is what makes lenders demand a premium.
questions.kr: 완전히 예상된(기대) 인플레이션은 임금 협상·계약 가격에 반영 가능 → 피해가 적음. 예상 밖 인플레이션은 정의상 반영되지 않은 부분; 불확실한 인플레이션은 대출자가 프리미엄을 요구하게 만드는 것.

questions.stem: The transactions demand for money refers to the demand to hold money:

choices.A: as a buffer against unforeseen events that require cash
choices.B: to use in the purchase of goods and services
choices.C: based on the opportunities and risks of other financial instruments

questions.explanation: Three options = three motives' definitions; the question attaches ONE label. Transactions = PURCHASES of goods and services. A is the PRECAUTIONARY motive (unforeseen / buffer); C is the SPECULATIVE motive (other assets' risk and return). Anchor each motive to its keyword and locate that keyword first.
questions.kr: 세 선지 = 세 동기의 정의; 라벨 하나를 붙이는 문제. 거래적 = 재화·서비스 '구매'. A는 예비적 동기(예상 밖/완충), C는 투기적 동기(다른 자산의 위험·수익). 동기마다 키워드를 고정하고 그 키워드부터 찾는다.

questions.stem: An expansion in the money supply would most likely:

choices.A: lead to a decline in nominal interest rates
choices.B: lead to a rise in nominal interest rates
choices.C: reduce the equilibrium amount of money agents wish to hold

questions.explanation: MS shifts right → money more plentiful → less valuable → its price, the interest rate, FALLS (and the price level rises). B is the polarity flip. C is wrong twice: the equilibrium quantity of money held RISES (someone must hold the new money), and MD did not move — the economy slides down along MD. First-order effect of more supply in any market: a lower price. Trace 'M ↑ → i ↓ → P ↑' before reading options.
questions.kr: MS 우측 이동 → 돈이 흔해져 가치↓ → 돈의 가격인 금리 '하락'(물가는 상승). B는 극성 반대. C는 두 번 틀림: 균형 화폐 보유량은 '증가'(새 돈은 누군가 보유), MD는 움직이지 않고 MD 곡선을 따라 이동. 어느 시장이든 공급 증가의 1차 효과는 가격 하락. 선지 읽기 전 'M↑ → i↓ → P↑'를 먼저 쓴다.

questions.stem: Monetary policy is best described as:

choices.A: the setting of medium-term targets for broad money aggregates
choices.B: central bank activities aimed at influencing the quantity of money and credit in the economy
choices.C: the central bank's management of the government's budget deficit

questions.explanation: The definition names the ACTOR (central bank) and the LEVER (money and credit) with the purpose of influencing economic activity. A money-aggregate target is a TOOL of monetary policy, not its definition; the budget deficit belongs to FISCAL policy (wrong actor). Tool / use / objective options are the standard distractors on definition stems.
questions.kr: 정의는 '주체'(중앙은행)와 '수단'(통화·신용)을 명시하고 목적은 경제활동 조절. 통화량 목표는 통화정책의 '도구'이지 정의가 아님; 재정적자는 '재정정책'(주체 오류). 도구·용도·목표 선지는 정의 문제의 표준 오답.

questions.stem: Fiscal policy is best described as the government's decisions about:

choices.A: taxation and spending
choices.B: redistributing income and wealth
choices.C: balancing the budget each year

questions.explanation: Fiscal policy = decisions about taxation and spending, used to regulate economic activity. Redistribution is a SECONDARY use that fiscal policy can additionally serve; annual budget balance is a possible OBJECTIVE, not the definition.
questions.kr: 재정정책 = 조세와 지출에 관한 결정, 경제활동 조절이 목적. 재분배는 '부수적 용도', 매년 균형재정은 '가능한 목표'일 뿐 정의가 아님.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in any measure of the money supply?

choices.A: Balances in current (checking) accounts
choices.B: Notes and coins held by the public
choices.C: Payments made with a credit card

questions.explanation: A credit-card payment is a deferred payment — a loan from the card issuer — not a transfer of an existing money balance, so it is not money. Deposits drawn by cheque or debit card are money; notes and coins are money. NOT stem: T/F each option.
questions.kr: 신용카드 결제는 지급 이연(카드사의 대출)이지 기존 통화 잔액의 이전이 아니므로 통화가 아님. 수표·직불카드로 인출되는 예금과 지폐·주화는 통화. NOT 지문: 선지별 T/F.

questions.concept: Store of wealth depends on belief
questions.stem: Gold's ability to serve as a store of wealth most directly depends on:

choices.A: its physical durability alone
choices.B: the belief that others will continue to value it
choices.C: its being difficult to counterfeit

questions.explanation: Durability helps, but the curriculum stresses that the store-of-wealth function rests on continued DEMAND — the belief that others will keep valuing gold (ornaments, jewellery). If gold were valued less each year it would fail as a store of wealth and could lose its medium-of-exchange status too. Hard to counterfeit is one of the five medium-of-exchange qualities, not the store-of-wealth basis.
questions.kr: 내구성도 도움이 되지만 교재는 가치저장 기능이 지속적인 '수요'(남들이 계속 가치를 인정한다는 믿음)에 달려 있다고 강조. 매년 가치가 떨어지면 가치저장 기능을 잃고 교환매개 지위도 잃을 수 있음. 위조 어려움은 교환매개의 5가지 성질 중 하나.

questions.stem: A bank receives a new deposit of 250. With a reserve requirement of 12.5%, the total amount of money that can be created in the banking system is closest to:
questions.explanation: Total money created = deposit / reserve requirement = 250 / 0.125 = 2,000 — the curriculum's convention INCLUDES the original deposit (sum of all deposits). Choice A (1,750) subtracts the initial deposit, which is only right when the stem says 'additional' or 'beyond the deposit'; choice C is the first bank's reserve.
questions.kr: 총 창출 통화 = 예금/지급준비율 = 250/0.125 = 2,000 — 교재 관례는 최초 예금 '포함'(모든 예금의 합). A(1,750)는 최초 예금을 뺀 값으로 '추가/beyond'라고 할 때만 정답; C는 첫 은행의 준비금.

questions.stem: Regarding the link between money growth and inflation, the curriculum most likely states that:

choices.A: money growth necessarily causes inflation in every economy
choices.B: causality may also run from real economic activity to the money supply
choices.C: velocity rises proportionally with the money supply

questions.explanation: Monetarists read causality as money growth → inflation, but the curriculum's caveat is that it may run the other way: the quantity of money may be DETERMINED BY the level of economic activity. 'Necessarily' overstates the position (absolute claim); velocity is assumed roughly CONSTANT, not proportional to M.
questions.kr: 통화주의자는 통화증가 → 인플레이션이라 보지만, 교재는 인과관계가 반대(경제활동 수준이 통화량을 결정)일 수도 있다고 단서를 닮. '반드시'는 과장(절대적 주장); 유통속도는 M에 비례하는 게 아니라 대략 '일정'하다고 가정.

questions.concept: Money demand curve — why downward sloping
questions.stem: The demand-for-money curve slopes downward against the nominal interest rate most likely because, as rates rise:

choices.A: the transactions demand for money falls
choices.B: the speculative demand for money falls
choices.C: the money supply contracts

questions.explanation: Higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding money instead of bonds, so SPECULATIVE balances fall — that is the curriculum's stated reason for the downward slope. Transactions demand is tied to GDP, not the rate; money supply is a separate, vertical curve (fixed nominal amount).
questions.kr: 금리 상승 = 채권 대신 현금을 보유하는 기회비용 상승 → '투기적' 잔액 감소 — 교재가 말하는 우하향의 이유. 거래적 수요는 GDP에 연동, 통화공급은 별도의 수직선(고정된 명목량).

questions.stem: According to the Fisher effect, an increase in expected inflation most likely leads to:

choices.A: a higher nominal interest rate with the real rate unchanged
choices.B: a higher real interest rate with the nominal rate unchanged
choices.C: lower nominal and real interest rates

questions.explanation: R_nom = R_real + πᵉ with the REAL rate stable over time → changes in nominal rates reflect changes in EXPECTED inflation one-for-one. Money neutrality underlies this: money affects inflation (and so nominal rates) but not the real rate.
questions.kr: 명목 = 실질 + 기대인플레이션, 실질금리는 안정 → 명목금리 변화는 기대인플레이션 변화를 1:1로 반영. 화폐 중립성이 배경: 통화는 인플레이션(명목금리)에는 영향, 실질금리에는 없음.

questions.stem: Highly volatile and unpredictable inflation most likely affects investment by:

choices.A: lowering borrowing costs as lenders seek safe borrowers
choices.B: raising borrowing costs because lenders demand a premium for inflation uncertainty
choices.C: leaving borrowing costs unchanged because contracts are indexed

questions.explanation: Uncertain inflation makes lenders demand a PREMIUM → borrowing costs rise → investment and activity are discouraged. This is the risk-premium component of the nominal rate (real + expected inflation + uncertainty premium). Indexation (choice C) is the hypothetical 'world 1' in which agents would be indifferent — not the real-world case.
questions.kr: 불확실한 인플레이션 → 대출자가 '프리미엄' 요구 → 차입비용 상승 → 투자·활동 위축. 명목금리의 위험 프리미엄 구성요소(실질 + 기대인플레 + 불확실성 프리미엄). 완전 물가연동(C)은 가상의 '세계 1'일 뿐 현실이 아님.

questions.stem: If inflation turns out higher than anticipated over the life of a fixed-rate loan, the most likely result is:

choices.A: the borrower gains because the real value of the debt declines
choices.B: the lender gains because nominal repayments rise
choices.C: no transfer, since both parties expected inflation

questions.explanation: Nominal debt is fixed; surprise inflation erodes the real value of what the borrower repays → borrower gains, lender loses. Nominal repayments on a fixed-rate loan do NOT rise (B is false). Both parties expected SOME inflation, but the transfer comes from the UNEXPECTED part.
questions.kr: 명목 부채 고정; 예상 밖 인플레이션은 차입자가 갚는 실질가치를 잠식 → 차입자 이득, 대출자 손해. 고정금리 대출의 명목 상환액은 오르지 않음(B 거짓). 양측이 어느 정도 인플레이션을 예상했어도 이전은 '예상 밖' 부분에서 발생.

questions.front: Monetary policy vs fiscal policy — exact curriculum definitions, actor, lever, and the four distractor types
questions.back:
MONETARY = central bank activities directed toward influencing the quantity of MONEY AND CREDIT. FISCAL = the government's decisions about TAXATION AND SPENDING. Both regulate activity (accelerate when slow, moderate when overheating); fiscal can ALSO redistribute income/wealth.
Distractors: a TOOL (money-aggregate targets), a wrong ACTOR (central bank running the deficit), a secondary USE (redistribution), an OBJECTIVE (balancing the budget yearly).

questions.front: The three functions of money, the five medium-of-exchange qualities (A-K-D-W-C), and the four barter problems
questions.back:
Functions: (1) medium of exchange, (2) store of wealth — depends on BELIEF others keep valuing it, (3) unit of account / measure of value.
Qualities: readily Acceptable, Known value, easily Divisible, high value-to-Weight, hard to Counterfeit.
Barter problems: double coincidence of wants; indivisibility; not wanting to exchange everything; no common measure of value.

questions.front: Money multiplier and total money created — formulas, the Exhibit 1 numbers, direction, and the three traps
questions.back:
Money multiplier = 1 / reserve requirement. Total money created = new deposit / reserve requirement (SUM of all deposits, original INCLUDED). €100 at 10% → multiplier 10, total €1,000 (100 + 90 + 81 + …). £100 at 5% → £2,000.
Smaller requirement → larger multiplier → more money.
Traps: subtract the original deposit ONLY if the stem says 'additional / beyond / new loans'; multiplier (10) ≠ total (1,000); 10% enters as 0.10.
Narrow money = notes & coins + very liquid deposits; broad = + all liquid assets usable for purchases. Credit cards are NOT money (deferred payment).

questions.front: Quantity equation, money neutrality, and the Fisher effect — formulas and what each implies
questions.back:
M × V = P × Y (identity; V = nominal GDP / M). Theory: V ≈ constant → PY proportional to M.
Neutrality: M ↑ with V, Y unchanged → P ↑ proportionally (M = 500, V = 4, Y = 1,000 → P = 2; M +10% → P +10%). Caveat: causality may run activity → money.
Fisher: R_nom = R_real + πᵉ (EXPECTED inflation). Real rate stable → nominal moves with inflation expectations. Full version adds a risk premium for inflation uncertainty. 2% + 3% = 5%; 6.5% − 2.5% = 4%.

questions.front: Three money-demand motives with their keywords; the money-market diagram and both adjustment chains
questions.back:
TRANSACTIONS = purchases (grows with GDP). PRECAUTIONARY = buffer against UNFORESEEN events (grows with GDP). SPECULATIVE = other assets' RISK (↑ → more money) and expected RETURN (↑ → less money).
MS vertical (fixed nominal amount); MD downward (speculative demand falls as rates rise).
Rate ABOVE equilibrium → excess SUPPLY of money → BUY bonds → bond prices ↑ → rates ↓. Rate BELOW → excess DEMAND → SELL bonds → prices ↓ → rates ↑.
Money supply ↑ → interest rate ↓ → price level ↑ (equilibrium money held RISES; movement along MD).

questions.front: Expected vs unexpected inflation — who wins/loses, the uncertainty premium, and the TV-manufacturer mechanism
questions.back:
Expected inflation is priced into wages and contracts → little harm. UNEXPECTED inflation redistributes: higher than expected → BORROWERS gain (real debt falls); lower than expected → LENDERS gain. Chain from 'nominal debt is fixed'.
Uncertain inflation → lenders demand a premium → borrowing costs ↑ → investment ↓.
TV manufacturer: a general +10% read as a relative-price signal → overexpansion → surplus → layoffs. Unanticipated inflation REDUCES THE INFORMATION CONTENT OF PRICES → exacerbates/causes booms and busts → controlling inflation is a main policy goal.

questions.stem: As the reserve requirement rises, the money multiplier most likely:

choices.A: increases
choices.B: decreases
choices.C: is unchanged

questions.explanation: Money multiplier = 1 / reserve requirement — an inverse relationship. A higher requirement means banks lend a smaller share of each deposit, so less money is created (1/0.10 = 10 → 1/0.20 = 5).
questions.kr: 통화승수 = 1/지급준비율 — 역관계. 준비율이 높으면 예금 중 대출 비율이 줄어 통화 창출 감소(1/0.10 = 10 → 1/0.20 = 5).

questions.stem: Which statement about the demand for money is most accurate?

choices.A: Precautionary money demand is directly related to GDP
choices.B: Transactions money demand is inversely related to returns on bonds
choices.C: Speculative money demand is inversely related to the perceived risk of other assets

questions.explanation: Three motives, three drivers: TRANSACTIONS and PRECAUTIONARY balances both grow with GDP (volume and value of transactions); SPECULATIVE balances are inversely related to other assets' expected RETURN and directly related to their perceived RISK. B attaches the speculative driver (bond returns) to the transactions label; C flips the risk direction. Check the motive's keyword before the direction word.
questions.kr: 세 동기, 세 결정요인: 거래적·예비적 잔액은 GDP(거래량·거래액)와 함께 증가; 투기적 잔액은 다른 자산의 기대수익과 역관계, 인지 위험과 정관계. B는 투기적 요인(채권 수익률)을 거래적 라벨에 붙임; C는 위험의 방향을 뒤집음. 방향 단어보다 동기의 키워드를 먼저 확인.

questions.concept: Excess supply of money on the diagram
questions.stem: On the money-market diagram (MD downward sloping, MS vertical at M₀, equilibrium at I₀), an excess supply of money exists when the nominal interest rate is:

choices.A: at I₀
choices.B: above I₀ (I₁)
choices.C: below I₀ (I₂)

questions.explanation: At a rate ABOVE equilibrium, the quantity of money demanded (M₁) is below the fixed supply (M₀) → excess supply of M₀ − M₁. Agents buy bonds with the surplus balances → bond prices rise → the rate falls back to I₀. Below I₀ the opposite holds (excess demand M₂ − M₀, bonds sold, rate rises).
questions.kr: 금리가 균형 위이면 화폐수요량(M₁)이 고정 공급(M₀)보다 작음 → M₀ − M₁만큼 초과공급. 잉여 잔액으로 채권 매수 → 채권가격↑ → 금리는 I₀로 하락. I₀ 아래에서는 반대(초과수요 M₂ − M₀, 채권 매도, 금리 상승).

questions.stem: According to money neutrality, money-supply growth leaves real variables such as output and employment unaffected in:

choices.A: the long run
choices.B: the short run
choices.C: both the long run and the short run

questions.explanation: Neutrality is a LONG-RUN proposition: a money increase ultimately raises the price level and leaves real variables unchanged. In the short run money is NOT neutral — which is precisely why monetary policy can influence the economy at all.
questions.kr: 중립성은 '장기' 명제: 통화 증가는 결국 물가만 올리고 실질변수는 불변. 단기에는 중립적이지 '않음' — 그래서 통화정책이 경제에 영향을 줄 수 있음.

questions.stem: A fundamental assumption behind using monetary policy to influence the economy is best described as:

choices.A: financial markets are efficient
choices.B: money is not neutral in the short run
choices.C: official interest rates do not affect exchange rates

questions.explanation: If money were neutral in the short run, changing the money supply would move only prices and monetary policy could not affect real activity. So the whole enterprise rests on SHORT-RUN non-neutrality (long-run neutrality is the Fisher/quantity-theory backdrop). 'Efficient markets' is a portfolio-theory phrase, not part of this reading — an off-model lure; C is simply false (rates do move exchange rates).
questions.kr: 단기에 화폐가 중립적이라면 통화량 변화는 물가만 움직여 통화정책이 실질활동에 영향을 못 줌. 따라서 전제는 '단기 비중립성'(장기 중립성은 피셔·화폐수량설의 배경). '효율적 시장'은 포트폴리오 이론 용어로 이 리딩에 없는 선지; C는 그냥 거짓(금리는 환율에 영향).

questions.stem: Monetarists most likely believe that:

choices.A: causality runs from inflation to the money supply
choices.B: inflation can be affected by changing the money-supply growth rate
choices.C: rapid financial innovation makes monetary policy more effective

questions.explanation: By definition, monetarists hold that prices can be controlled by controlling money-supply growth: causality money → inflation. A reverses the direction (that reverse causality is the curriculum's CAVEAT, not the monetarist view). Financial innovation makes money harder to define and policy harder, not easier.
questions.kr: 정의상 통화주의자는 통화 증가율 조절로 물가를 통제할 수 있다고 봄: 인과 통화 → 인플레이션. A는 방향 반대(역인과는 교재의 '단서'이지 통화주의 견해가 아님). 금융혁신은 통화 정의를 어렵게 해 정책을 더 어렵게 만듦.

questions.stem: The proposition that the real interest rate is relatively stable over time is most closely associated with:

choices.A: the Fisher effect
choices.B: money neutrality
choices.C: the quantity theory of money

questions.explanation: The Fisher effect IS the proposition that the real rate is stable, so changes in nominal rates reflect changes in expected inflation (R_nom = R_real + πᵉ). Money neutrality and the quantity theory are the related background (money affects prices, not real things), but the real-rate statement is Fisher's own claim. Adjacent concept ≠ the named concept — match the proposition to its owner.
questions.kr: 피셔 효과 자체가 '실질금리는 안정적이므로 명목금리 변화는 기대인플레이션 변화를 반영한다'는 명제(명목 = 실질 + πᵉ). 화폐 중립성·화폐수량설은 배경(통화는 물가에만 영향)이지만 실질금리 안정성 명제의 주인은 피셔. 인접 개념 ≠ 지목된 개념.

questions.stem: Which equation follows from the Fisher effect?

choices.A: Nominal rate = real rate + expected inflation
choices.B: Real rate = nominal rate + expected inflation
choices.C: Nominal rate = real rate + market risk premium

questions.explanation: R_nom = R_real + πᵉ. B has the sign wrong (real = nominal − expected inflation); C substitutes a risk premium for expected inflation — the fuller decomposition adds an inflation-UNCERTAINTY premium on top, but the Fisher relation itself is real + expected inflation.
questions.kr: 명목 = 실질 + 기대인플레이션. B는 부호 오류(실질 = 명목 − 기대인플레이션); C는 기대인플레이션 자리에 위험 프리미엄을 넣음 — 확장형은 인플레이션 '불확실성' 프리미엄을 추가하지만 피셔 관계 자체는 실질 + 기대인플레이션.

questions.concept: Which inflation central banks worry about
questions.stem: Central banks are typically most concerned with the costs of:

choices.A: low levels of inflation that are anticipated
choices.B: moderate levels of inflation that are anticipated
choices.C: moderate levels of inflation that are not anticipated

questions.explanation: Unanticipated inflation carries the greater costs — wealth transfers between borrowers and lenders, an uncertainty premium in borrowing costs, and corrupted price signals — whereas anticipated inflation is priced into wages and contracts. Of the anticipated options, moderate inflation is less costly than very low inflation (the ~2% buffer against deflation), so A is not the answer either.
questions.kr: 예상 밖 인플레이션의 비용이 더 큼 — 차입자·대출자 간 부의 이전, 차입비용의 불확실성 프리미엄, 가격 신호 왜곡 — 반면 예상된 인플레이션은 임금·계약에 반영됨. 예상된 것 중에서는 완만한 인플레이션이 매우 낮은 인플레이션보다 비용이 적음(디플레이션 완충용 ~2%)이라 A도 아님.
